# Fairstay Collections (`fairstay-collections`)

Nursing-home collections: ages open receivables by payer type and says why each account is stuck (filing limit missed or near, credit balance, denial, no follow-up, not billed, Medicaid pending), as a monthly status report. Resident identifiers are masked before results reach the model.

**Fairstay Collections never writes off, adjusts or refunds a balance. Fairstay Collections does not log in to payer portals.**

Fairstay ver 1 · Collections and appeals · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · resident and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairstay-core`](../fairstay-core)

```bash
npx -y fairstay-collections demo
npx -y fairstay-collections mcp --root ./facility-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional Cedar Hollow receivables, aged on 2026-03-31. Planted:

- R1007: Medicare A from February 2025, never billed, so the one-year filing limit has passed.
- R1002: managed care for December, never billed, with a 90-day limit ending today.
- R1004: a private pay credit balance of 850.
- R1005: a managed care denial with reason code CO-197.
- R1001: billed 4 February with no follow-up since.
- R1003: Medicaid, last worked 10 January.
- R1008: March Medicaid days not billed yet.
- R1006: Medicaid pending.
- R1009: a current private pay balance that needs nothing.

[`rules-typo.json`](fixtures/rules-typo.json) misspells a setting, so the check refuses it.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `collections_check` | Age open receivables by payer type and list stuck accounts, most urgent first. | runs |
| `collections_write_report` | Write collections.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and collections.html into out_dir (default evergreen-out/collections). | runs |
| `collections_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `collections_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `collections_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `collections_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `claim_write_off` | Fairstay Collections never writes off, adjusts or refunds a balance. | refused |
| `payer_portal_login` | Fairstay Collections does not log in to payer portals. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `collections_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `ar` (required) | Open receivables (aged trial balance) under --root: resident, payer, service dates, billed date, balance, last follow-up, status note |
| `rules` | Optional rules JSON: follow_up_days, warn_days, bill_lag_days, filing_days |
| `as_of` | Aging date (YYYY-MM-DD, default today) |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold resident or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairstay-collections inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Open receivables (`ar`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `resident_id` | text (masked) | Resident ID, Resident #, Resident Number, Res ID, Res #, MRN, Medical Record Number, Client ID |
| `resident_name` | text (masked) | Resident, Resident Name, Name, Patient, Patient Name, Client Name, Resident Full Name |
| `payer` (required) | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Pay Source, Payer Source, Payor, Payor Name, Insurance |
| `payer_type` | text | Payer Type, Payor Type, Payer Class, Payer Category, Pay Type |
| `claim_id` | text | Claim ID, Claim #, Invoice, Invoice #, ICN, Claim Number, Reference |
| `from` | date | From, Start, Start Date, Effective Date, Begin Date, From Date, Admit Date, Service From |
| `to` | date | To, End, End Date, Thru, Through, Thru Date, Through Date, To Date |
| `billed_on` | date | Billed, Billed On, Bill Date, Billed Date, Submitted, Submit Date |
| `balance` (required) | amount | Balance, Open Balance, Outstanding, Amount Due, Balance Due, Amount |
| `last_follow_up` | date | Last Follow Up, Last Follow-up, Follow Up Date, Last Contact, Last Worked |
| `note` | text (masked) | Note, Notes, Status, Claim Status, Comment, Denial Reason |

## Settings file (`collections_rules`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `follow_up_days` | Flag balances not worked for this many days (default 30) |
| `warn_days` | Warn this many days before a filing limit (default 30) |
| `bill_lag_days` | Days after service before an unbilled balance is flagged (default 10) |
| `filing_days` | Filing limit in days by payer type, from your payer contracts and state rules |

## Memory

`collections_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `collections_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|
| `filing_limit` | is listed with results for staff to copy into the rules file. It never changes a check by itself. |

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairstay-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairstay-collections": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairstay-collections",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/facility-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairstay-collections -- npx -y fairstay-collections mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairstay-collections tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairstay-collections sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairstay-collections inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairstay-collections call collections_check '{"ar":"<ar>"}'
fairstay-collections eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairstay-collections demo
```

## Resident and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: resident and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to PointClickCare, MatrixCare, a payer portal, a bank, a state Medicaid portal or a payroll system.
- Medicare, Medicaid and payroll rules are summarised from public material as of 2026 and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, payroll or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, tax, accounting, clinical, reimbursement or HIPAA advice. A person decides what to bill, pay, appeal, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
